title: We are men like you (Acts 14)
hookLine: a crowd brings garlands and oxen to worship two travelers, and the travelers tear their clothes
tomorrow: one question could split the church. who settles it, and how?

cards: A standing ovation, a comment section calling someone a legend, a fan account with their face on it: praise is easy to soak up. In Lystra, a man who has never walked sits listening.
Paul says with a loud voice, "Stand upright on thy feet. And he leaped and walked." The crowd erupts in their own language: "The gods are come down to us in the likeness of men."
They decide Barnabas is Jupiter, and Paul is Mercurius, "because he was the chief speaker." A priest arrives with oxen and garlands. A sacrifice is about to begin, in their honor.

teach.b: Today's question: what are we, standing next to God? Barnabas and Paul answer with their clothes.

teach.h: MEN OF LIKE PASSIONS WITH YOU.
teach.b: "They rent their clothes, and ran in among the people," crying out: "Sirs, why do ye these things? We also are men of like passions with you." Like passions: the same feelings, the same needs.

Then Paul starts with what the crowd already knows: God "left not himself without witness, in that he did good, and gave us rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness."

Rain, harvest, a full table, shared by everyone in that square. Then the crowd turns, and Paul is stoned and left for dead; "he rose up, and came into the city." A neighbor tradition says the same thing in its own words.

teach.h: THE QUR'AN: A HUMAN BEING LIKE YOU.
teach.b: In the Qur'an, God tells the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, to say plainly that he is only a human being like his hearers, and that what is revealed to him is that their God is one God.
Two messengers, refusing to be made more than human, and pointing past themselves. Here's the honest difference. Christians, in this same book, worship Jesus as Lord, the Son of God.
Muslims honor Jesus as a prophet and a human messenger, and give worship to God alone. Not the same faith.
The same line: we are like you.

how: In Christian teaching worship belongs to God, not to apostles or preachers; Paul and Barnabas at Lystra are a story some churches tell about refusing praise that belongs to God.

games.q: what does “we are men like you” mean?
o: Paul and Barnabas refusing to be worshiped
the disciples arguing over who was greatest
a crowd honoring heroes after a victory

games.q: a Muslim classmate says the Qur'an calls the Prophet Muhammad a human being like everyone else, and asks if Christians have anything like that. what fits today?
o: yes: at Lystra, Paul and Barnabas said, we also are men of like passions with you.
no: Christians teach that their apostles were more than human.
yes, and it means Christians and Muslims believe the same about Jesus.
games.why: shared ground: messengers refusing to be worshiped. honest difference: Christians worship Jesus as Lord, and Muslims honor him as a prophet. alike, not the same.

practice: Bring to mind some credit you got that wasn't only yours: a teammate's idea, a parent's sacrifice, a teacher's patience. Write that person a short text handing the credit back, plain and specific.
Hold it for the sit, and send it when it feels right.

wordCard.voice: We are men like you. Paul and Barnabas at Lystra, tearing their clothes rather than be worshiped.

orig.note: Greek: of like passions, the word in Acts 14:15, men of like passions with you.

carryVoice: Keep this line: we are like you, said to a crowd still holding the garlands. Peace to you.
